subject: Clarify retroactive billing window applied to July usage
messages:
From: Elena Ramos <elena.ramos@opslytics.com>

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 25 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify retroactive billing window applied to July usage

Hi Karthik,

We're reaching out because our July invoice shows an unexpected ~120k token uplift compared to prior months and the usage export you provided last week. Attached are: opslytics_usage_export.csv (our internal token tally) and the Redwood invoice (redwood_invoice_2027-07.pdf).

Quick summary: the invoice appears to include the same sessions twice for a subset of long-running conversations that cross midnight UTC on July 1 and July 15. We suspect a retroactive change to a billing/aggregation window caused duplicate attribution. Can you confirm whether any metering window or attribution rule changed during July?

Asks:
- Please pause collection/collections for invoice 2027-07 while you audit.
- Provide a short explanation of the root cause and a timeline for reconciliation.
- If this is a metering error, we'd like a provisional credit applied and the corrected invoice before our month-end close.

I've CC'd our finance mailbox (opslytics-billing@opslytics.com) and Kimberly from our billing team.

Thanks,
Elena Ramos
Finance Operations | OpsLytics
elena.ramos@opslytics.com

Attachment: redwood_invoice_2027-07.pdf (PDF, 3 pages)

Immediate plan: I’ve looped in Ben (billing) and Kimberly (account finance) to validate metering and invoice state. Ben, can you confirm whether there was any change to aggregation windows or attribution rules in July and, if so, whether rollback or provisional credits are possible while we investigate?

I’ll put the invoice on hold internally while we triage (won’t stop customer-side collection entirely until we confirm). Expect an update within 48 business hours.

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Lauren Bennett <lauren_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Jul 2027 10:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify retroactive billing window applied to July usage

Hi all — quick status from billing side after an initial sweep.

What we see: on July 1 at 00:00 UTC we deployed a minor change to how we align session attribution windows for accounts that have non-UTC timezone preferences. The intent was to avoid splitting long-running chats across billing days by aligning to the customer's preferred TZ. For most customers it reduced fragmentation, but for a small number (including OpsLytics) a subset of long-lived sessions that started before the change and continued after got attributed twice due to an off-by-one overlap in the window boundary logic.

Sample evidence (from our telemetry):
- session_id: S-71c3a9b2 — tokens attributed July 1 23:58:14 -> 00:10:03 (both pre- and post-deploy windows)
- session_id: S-82f4b018 — tokens show duplicate attribution on July 15 boundary

Immediate remediation:
1) We can generate a targeted re-aggregation for the affected session IDs and produce an adjusted token report.
2) We will apply a provisional credit for the duplicated tokens while we complete the re-aggregation (suggesting provisional credit of $2,300 based on our rough delta).
3) We will place the invoice 2027-07 on hold for collection pending final reconciliation.

Ben — please proceed with creating the re-aggregation job and share the meter sample (metering-sample-opslytics.csv) once ready.

Ben Carter
Billing Manager | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
Attachment: metering-sample-opslytics.csv (CSV, 120 rows)

We also request:
- A short remediation note explaining what changed so we can communicate internally.
- Confirmation the July invoice is on hold and not in collections while this is open.

Subject: Re: Clarify retroactive billing window applied to July usage

Elena — quick reconciliation update and next steps: thanks for the session ids. Ben’s team completed targeted re-aggregation and produced an adjusted usage report. Summary:

- Root cause: off-by-one overlap when switching the per-account aggregation boundary to local timezone; affected ~0.9% of OpsLytics' July token total.
- Action taken: re-aggregation completed, duplicate attributions removed.
- Financial remediation: provisional credit of $2,300 issued against invoice 2027-07. The invoice is marked On Hold internally; collections have been paused while final confirmation is issued.
- Timeline: we’ll send the final corrected invoice and reconciliation spreadsheet by EOD Friday (5 business days) and remove the hold if numbers reconcile. If anything remains outstanding after your review we’ll escrow the disputed portion until final sign-off.

Related ticket: BILL-4821 (internal) — https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/BILL-4821
HubSpot record: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/company/opslytics

- Kimberly / Lauren: confirm the credit posting and update AR status.
- Elena: review adjusted report and confirm receipt.

Thanks again for the prompt examples — that made the audit fast. I’ll follow up if anything else pops up.

Best,
